 Hundreds of Thousands Losing Their ACA Insurer for 2027 Could Be Auto-Matched to Plans They Never Chose
 Published Oct 24, 2026 10:47 AM EDT 
 By
 Joseph James 
 Joe Raedle | Getty Images 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 HealthCare.gov will have 152 participating insurers in 2027, down 14% from this year, according to CMS documents reported by The Washington Sun on Oct. 16. A separate tally from healthinsurance.org , last updated Oct. 8, counts at least a dozen insurers leaving marketplaces after 2026, led by Cigna's exit from all 11 states where it sells marketplace plans.
 For affected households, the urgent question is not only price. People whose insurer is leaving will often be moved automatically into a plan from another company if they do nothing, and that plan may use different doctors, hospitals and drug lists.
 The federal figures also suggest most shoppers will still have choices. The average HealthCare.gov enrollee will have plans from five or six insurers, the Sun reported, and average monthly premiums for the most popular plans are set to rise 11%. Those figures cover the 29 states that use HealthCare.gov rather than their own marketplaces.
 Cigna's Exit Leads a Longer List Than First Reported
 MedicalDaily previously reported on seven insurers leaving 2027 markets in 20 states , based on a Commonwealth Fund analysis. The fuller healthinsurance.org list adds more carriers, and the CMS documents add a federal count of the insurers that remain.
 Cigna, which covers about 369,000 marketplace enrollees, is leaving the marketplaces in Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Virginia. Baylor Scott & White Health Plan, which covers about 100,000 marketplace enrollees in Texas, is also leaving.
 Other exits include CareSource in Indiana, Ohio and West Virginia; PacificSource in Idaho, Montana and Oregon; Providence Health Plan in Oregon; Medica in Iowa, Kansas and Oklahoma; and UnitedHealthcare in Georgia. Molina is leaving Illinois, Ohio, Mississippi and Kentucky and plans to shrink its individual market footprint from 14 states to six, though not all of its exit states are clear yet. Healthinsurance.org says the exits affect hundreds of thousands of enrollees across multiple states.
 Automatic Reassignment Has Limits Families Should Know
 When an insurer leaves, the marketplace generally tries to prevent a coverage gap. If your insurance company is not offering any similar plans next year, HealthCare.gov says, "we'll re-enroll you in a comparable one with a different insurance company." A letter from your insurer explains your coverage options.
 A comparable plan is not guaranteed to include the same doctors, hospitals, or prescriptions. That is where household risk comes in. A parent whose child sees a specialist, a person managing diabetes, or an older adult on several brand-name drugs could land in a plan where those providers or medicines are out of network or cost more.
 The rules are not the same everywhere. ConnectiCare Insurance Company enrollees in Connecticut will need to pick another insurer's plan themselves if they want to keep marketplace coverage, healthinsurance.org reports. State-run exchanges also set their own dates, and Oregon is moving from HealthCare.gov to its own Explore Health platform for 2027.
 KFF senior vice president Cynthia Cox described the premium picture to the Sun as "not great news but it's also not a collapse." Louise Norris, a health policy analyst at healthinsurance.org, urged even satisfied customers to compare plans during open enrollment, according to a healthinsurance.org release on 2027 marketplace changes .
 Costs, Deadlines, and a Checklist Before Dec. 15
 Prices are rising for a second straight year. Insurers proposed a median 15% increase for 2027, according to KFF's analysis of proposed 2027 premiums , and the enhanced federal premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025. Middle-income buyers who earn too much for subsidies carry the full increase.
 The out-of-pocket maximum for an individual plan rises to $12,000 in 2027, up from $10,600 in 2026. Starting with 2027 coverage, refugees, asylees, people with Temporary Protected Status, and people with work or student visas will no longer qualify for federal marketplace subsidies, according to healthinsurance.org. Those households should check their eligibility early rather than at the deadline.
 Open enrollment runs Nov. 1 to Jan. 15 on HealthCare.gov. Choosing a plan by Dec. 15 secures coverage starting Jan. 1, and HealthCare.gov says people who log in on or after Dec. 16 may see a message saying they were automatically re-enrolled. People can still switch plans until Jan. 15 for coverage starting Feb. 1.
 A simple household checklist can prevent surprises. Read every letter from your insurer and the marketplace, update your 2027 income estimate, and look up each doctor, hospital, and prescription in any plan you are considering. Compare total yearly cost, including the deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, not just the monthly premium.
 People with serious conditions or ongoing treatment should ask their care team which 2027 plans it accepts before choosing. Free help is available from marketplace navigators and assisters, and licensed brokers can also help compare plans. Current coverage stays in force through the end of the year as long as premiums are paid, so there is no reason to cancel early.
 CMS is expected to release its premium figures before open enrollment begins Nov. 1. Most shoppers will still have several insurers to choose from, but anyone whose carrier is leaving should treat an automatic match as a starting point, not a final answer, and check it before Dec. 15.

 Key Questions Answered
 Which insurers are leaving the ACA marketplace for 2027? 
 Cigna is leaving all 11 of its marketplace states. Other exits include Baylor Scott & White, CareSource, PacificSource, Providence, Medica, and UnitedHealthcare in Georgia, and Molina is shrinking its footprint.
 What happens if my insurer leaves and I do nothing? 
 HealthCare.gov will generally re-enroll you in a comparable plan from another insurer. That plan may not include your doctors or medications.
 When is open enrollment for 2027? 
 It runs Nov. 1 to Jan. 15 on HealthCare.gov. Pick a plan by Dec. 15 for coverage starting Jan. 1. State-run marketplaces may set different dates.
 Will I still have choices? 
 Most people will. Federal figures show the average HealthCare.gov enrollee will still have plans from five or six insurers.
 Where can I get free help? 
 Marketplace navigators and assisters listed on HealthCare.gov or your state exchange offer free enrollment help. Licensed brokers can also help compare plans.
